semantics: KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.incidenceGraph_adj_inl_inr: core; audit verified; a component is adjacent to a point it has a branch over
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.reachable_of_eqvGen: core; audit verified; components linked through the points are linked in the incidence graph
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.exists_one_le_of_one_le_sum: core; audit verified; a listed point lying on the curve lies on some component
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.incidenceGraph_connected: core; audit verified; a connected curve has a connected incidence graph
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.exists_pair_of_mem_edgeSet: core; audit verified; every incidence edge is a component–point pair with a branch
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_edgeSet_le_card_pairs: core; audit verified; the incidence edges inject into the pairs with a branch
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_pairs_add_one_le: core; audit verified; with a double branch somewhere, the pairs with a branch number at most Σb − 1
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.card_add_card_le_sum_branches: core; audit verified; a connected curve with a self-identification has c + |points| ≤ Σ_p r_p
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.euler_le_zero: core; audit verified; the Euler bound χ = c − Σ_p (r_p − 1) ≤ 0 for a connected curve with a self-identification

KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.connectedNonproper_implies_etaleMaximal: full; audit unapproved; connected nonproperness implies étale-maximality, with the audit's two prerequisites as explicit hypotheses: the Euler count χ(S_F) = c − Σ_p (r_p − 1) read off the A¹ normalisations (KG-P12 with additivity of the topological Euler characteristic) and the multibranch consequence of non-maximality (KG-EM02 with KG-EM03); from Jelonek's positivity as a Published axiom, verified once that input is admitted
KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.nonmaximal_implies_nonproperDisconnected: core; audit unapproved; the contrapositive, derived, carrying the same two hypotheses
value.statement: If the nonproperness curve S_F of a plane Keller map is connected then F is étale-maximal; equivalently, non-maximality forces S_F to be disconnected. Non-maximality gives a component with normalization A^1 and a multibranch self-identification, so χ(S_F) ≤ 0, against Jelonek's χ(S_F) > 0 for connected S_F.

research.author: packet 2026-09-14: LLM-derived, no claim-specific human check, no Lean kernel build
research.reason: highest-priority human audit; never to be described as Assi's theorem

semantics: KellerGroupoids.ProjectStatements.nonmaximal_implies_exactlyTwoNodalFibers: full; audit unapproved; derived from KG-EM07, KG-EM08, KG-EM09 and Assi's equinodal theorem exactly as the audit derives it, carrying KG-EM07's two hypotheses; rests on five Published axioms and no hole; verified once those inputs are admitted
value.statement: If a plane Keller map is not étale-maximal then S_F = C_0 ⊔ C_1 with C_i = V(h − a_i) the two exceptional rational members of a noncoordinate one-place pencil; each C_i is rational with one place at infinity, and both have the same positive number of affine singular points, all ordinary transverse nodes. The classification of the two fibers is Assi's; the reduction from Keller non-maximality to it is the project's.
